Reportedly, Apple has been co-developing "second-party" Home accessories with LG, but the latest leaks indicate that another company will also be launching "second-party" smart home products.

Code from iOS 27.2 reveals that, in addition to LG, other "second-party" Home accessories are set to launch.

Over the past day, we have seen multiple reports regarding Apple's ambitions to expand its smart home ecosystem.

In addition to the first-party Home products expected to launch next week — such as the next-generation Apple TV 4K, the "HomePad," and the HomePod mini 2 — the company is reportedly working with LG on a new lineup of home accessories.

These accessories are co-manufactured by Apple and LG, but will be sold under the LG brand. Images leaked today reveal what they look like:

  • Leaked images reveal new Home smart locks, thermostats, and more from the Apple-LG collaboration
  • Apple and LG's new Home camera and doorbell exposed in leaked images

It makes perfect sense for Apple to co-develop products to strengthen its smart home ecosystem, and that partnership may not be limited to LG alone.

Leaker pdfu has uncovered evidence in iOS 27.2 of two additional Home accessories, both likewise tagged as "second-party" products.

These accessories are a Schneider-branded smart thermostat and a temperature/humidity sensor.

As pdfu's post notes, currently in Apple's HomeKit database, only the new LG accessories and these two Schneider products carry the "second-party" tag.

Accessories classified as second-party will "receive special treatment from the operating system."

It remains unclear whether this means Apple is working as closely with Schneider on its accessories as it reportedly is with LG. But the code does suggest as much.

What do you think of Apple's reported new Home product strategy? Let us know in the comments.
